situationUz: Til kursidagi birinçi darsingiz. Öqituvçi siz bilan tanişmoqda.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Good morning! I’m Ms Brown, your teacher.
lines.uz: Xayrli tong! Men Braun xonim, sizning öqituvçingizman.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Good morning! My name ___ Aziz.

gap.whyUz: “My name” — bitta narsa (u), şuning uçun “is”: My name is…

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Nice to meet you, Aziz. Where are you from?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: I’m ___ Uzbekistan. I live in Tashkent.

gap.whyUz: Kelib çiqiş “from” bilan aytiladi: I’m from Uzbekistan.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Great. How old are you?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: I’m nineteen. Nice to ___ you too!
lines.uz: Ön töqqiz yoşdaman. Men ham tanişganimdan xursandman!

gap.whyUz: Birinçi tanişuvda qotib qolgan ibora: “Nice to meet you”.

note.titleUz: am / is / are — qaçon qaysi biri?
pointsUz: I → am (I’m).
he / she / it va bitta narsa (my name) → is.
you / we / they → are.

examples.en: I am a student.
My teacher is from London.
We are in class 3.

situationUz: Döstingiz telefoningizdagi oilaviy suratni körib, savol bermoqda.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: What a nice photo! Who is this woman?
lines.uz: Qanday çiroyli surat! Bu ayol kim?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: That’s ___ mother. Her name is Dilnoza.
lines.uz: Bu mening onam. Uning ismi Dilnoza.

gap.whyUz: Egalik “my” bilan: my mother — mening onam.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: And the tall man?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: He’s my ___. He is a doctor.

gap.whyUz: Erkak qarindoş — “brother” (aka/uka); “sister” — opa/singil.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Have you got any sisters?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Yes, I ___ got one sister. She is ten.
lines.uz: Ha, bitta singlim bor. U ön yoşda.

gap.whyUz: “I” bilan “have got” işlatiladi; “has got” — he/she uçun.

note.titleUz: Egalik: my / your / his / her va have got
pointsUz: my — mening, your — sizning, his — uning (erkak), her — uning (ayol).
I / you / we / they → have got; he / she → has got.

examples.en: This is my brother.
She has got two cats.

situationUz: Sinfdoşingiz siz bilan birga kutubxonaga boriş uçun vaqt söramoqda.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Let’s go to the library tomorrow. What time do you get up?
lines.uz: Ertaga kutubxonaga boraylik. Soat neçada turasiz?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: I usually get up ___ seven o’clock.

gap.whyUz: Soat bilan “at”: at seven o’clock, at 8:30.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: And when do you have breakfast?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: I ___ breakfast at half past seven.

gap.whyUz: Present Simple, “I” bilan fe’l özgarmaydi: I have breakfast.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: OK. Let’s meet at nine.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Great! See you ___.

gap.whyUz: Uçraşuv ertaga — “See you tomorrow”.

pointsUz: Har kungi odat: I get up, I have breakfast (fe’l özgarmaydi).
he / she bilan fe’lga -s qöşiladi: she gets up.
Soat → at, kun → on (on Monday), qism → in (in the morning).

examples.en: I go to school at eight.
She works on Saturdays.

situationUz: Ijaraga olingan kvartiraga keldingiz. Uy egasi xonalarni körsatmoqda.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Welcome! This is the living room.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: It’s nice. Is ___ a TV?

gap.whyUz: Biror narsa borligini söraş: Is there a…? / There is a…

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Yes, there is. It’s next to the window.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: And where are the keys? Are they ___ the table?

gap.whyUz: Sirt ustida — “on”: on the table. Içida — “in”: in the box.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: No, they are in the kitchen, in the drawer.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: How many bedrooms ___ there?

gap.whyUz: “bedrooms” — köplik, şuning uçun “are there”.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: There are two bedrooms and one bathroom.
lines.uz: Ikkita yotoqxona va bitta hammom bor.

note.titleUz: There is / there are va joy predloglari
pointsUz: Bitta narsa → there is; köp narsa → there are.
Savol: Is there…? / Are there…?
on — ustida, in — içida, next to — yonida, under — tagida.

examples.en: There is a lamp next to the bed.
Are there any chairs in the kitchen?

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Hello! What would you like?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: ___ I have a cup of tea, please?

gap.whyUz: Xuşmuomala sörov: “Can I have…, please?”

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Of course. Anything to eat?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Yes, I’d like ___ sandwich, please.

gap.whyUz: “sandwich” undoş tovuş bilan boşlanadi va sanaladi → a sandwich.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Sorry, we haven’t got any sandwiches today. We’ve got soup.
lines.uz: Keçirasiz, bugun sendviç yöq. Şörva bor.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: OK, some soup, then. How ___ is it?

gap.whyUz: Narx söraş: “How much is it?”

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: The tea and the soup are six dollars.

note.titleUz: Xuşmuomala buyurtma: Can I have… / I’d like…
pointsUz: “Can I have…, please?” va “I’d like…” — muloyim sörov.
Sanaladigan bittasi → a/an; sanalmaydigan → some (some soup, some water).
Narx: How much is it? / How much are they?

examples.en: Can I have some water, please?
I’d like an apple juice.

situationUz: Döstingiz şanba kuni kinoga borişni taklif qilmoqda.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: I’m going to watch a film on Saturday. Can you come?
lines.uz: Şanba kuni kino körmoqçiman. Kela olasanmi?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Sorry, I ___ come on Saturday. I work.
lines.uz: Keçir, şanba kuni kela olmayman. Işlayman.

gap.whyUz: Imkoniyat yöqligi “can’t” bilan: I can’t come.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: What about Sunday?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Sunday is OK. I’m going ___ visit my grandmother in the morning, but I’m free in the evening.
lines.uz: Yakşanba böladi. Ertalab buvimnikiga bormoqçiman, lekin keçqurun böşman.

gap.whyUz: Reja: be going TO + fe’l — I’m going to visit.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Great! Do you like comedies?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Yes, I love ___ comedies!
lines.uz: Ha, komediya körişni juda yaxşi köraman!

gap.whyUz: love / like dan keyin fe’l -ing bilan: I love watching…

note.titleUz: can / can’t va be going to
pointsUz: can / can’t + fe’l — qila oliş (I can swim, I can’t come).
Reja: am / is / are going to + fe’l.
like / love / hate + fe’l-ing.

examples.en: We are going to play football.
She can’t drive.

situationUz: Yangi şahardasiz va temir yöl vokzalini qidiryapsiz. Yölovçidan söraysiz.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Excuse me, ___ is the railway station?

gap.whyUz: Joy söraş — “where”: Where is…?

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Go straight on and turn left at the bridge.
lines.uz: Töğriga yuring va köprikda çapga buriling.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Turn left ___ the bridge. OK.

gap.whyUz: Aniq nuqtada buriliş — “at”: turn left at the bridge.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Then the station is on your right, next to the museum.
lines.uz: Keyin vokzal öng tomoningizda, muzey yonida.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Is it far? Yesterday I ___ lost here!
lines.uz: Uzoqmi? Keça şu yerda adaşib qolgandim!

gap.whyUz: Ötgan zamon, “I” bilan → was: I was lost.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: No, it’s about five minutes on foot.

note.titleUz: Yöl körsatiş iboralari va was / were
pointsUz: go straight on — töğriga yuring; turn left / right — çapga / öngga buriling.
on your left / right — çap / öng tomoningizda.
Ötgan zamon: I / he / she / it → was; you / we / they → were.

examples.en: The bank is on the left.
We were at home yesterday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Welcome back! How was your holiday?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: It was great, thanks. We ___ Samarkand for a week.
lines.uz: Zör ötdi, rahmat. Bir hafta Samarqandga borib keldik.

gap.whyUz: Tugagan voqea — Past Simple: visit + -ed = visited.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Lovely! What did you do there?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: We ___ around the old city and took lots of photos.
lines.uz: Eski şahar böylab sayr qildik va köp surat oldik.

gap.whyUz: Past Simple: walk → walked.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Did you like the food?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Yes, I ___. The plov was amazing!

gap.whyUz: Did you…? savoliga qisqa javob: Yes, I did / No, I didn’t.

note.titleUz: Past Simple: töğri fe’llar va qisqa javoblar
pointsUz: Töğri fe’l + -ed: visit → visited, walk → walked.
Savol: Did + ega + fe’lning 1-şakli? (Did you like…?)
Qisqa javob: Yes, I did. / No, I didn’t.

examples.en: We stayed in a small hotel.
Did she call you? — No, she didn’t.

situationUz: Yangi tanişingiz bilan bolalikdagi öyinlar haqida gaplaşyapsiz.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Where did you grow up?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: I grew up in a small village. Our house ___ near a river.
lines.uz: Kiçik qişloqda ösganman. Uyimiz daryo yonida edi.

gap.whyUz: Bitta uy, ötgan zamon → was.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: What games did you play?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: We ___ football every day after school.
lines.uz: Har kuni maktabdan keyin futbol öynardik.

gap.whyUz: play → played (y dan oldin unli bölsa, -ed oddiy qöşiladi).

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Who was your favourite teacher?
lines.uz: Eng yaxşi körgan öqituvçingiz kim edi?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Mr Karimov. He ___ us a lot about nature.
lines.uz: Karimov domla. U bizga tabiat haqida köp narsa örgatgan.

gap.whyUz: “teach” — notöğri fe’l: teach → taught.

pointsUz: Ba’zi fe’llar -ed olmaydi: grow → grew, teach → taught, go → went.
Ularni yodlaş kerak — har biri alohida şaklga ega.
I / he / she / it → was, you / we / they → were.

examples.en: I went to school by bus.
My parents were teachers.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Good afternoon. Where are you travelling to?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: To Bukhara. Which is ___, the train or the bus?
lines.uz: Buxoroga. Qaysi biri tezroq: poyezdmi yoki avtobus?

gap.whyUz: Ikki narsani soliştiriş: qisqa sifat + -er → faster.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: The fast train. It takes four hours.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Is it ___ expensive than the bus?

gap.whyUz: Uzun sifat bilan qiyos: more + sifat + than → more expensive than.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: A little. A return ticket is 200,000 sums.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: OK, one ___ ticket, please.

gap.whyUz: “return ticket” — borib-keliş; “single” — faqat bir tomonga.

pointsUz: Qisqa sifat + -er + than: cheap → cheaper than.
Uzun sifat: more + sifat + than: more comfortable than.
Eng: the + -est / the most (the fastest, the most expensive).

examples.en: The bus is cheaper than the train.
This is the most beautiful city.

situationUz: Döstingiz bilan hafta oxiri toğga çiqişni rejalaştiryapsiz.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: What are your plans for the weekend?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: I’m ___ to go hiking in the mountains.

gap.whyUz: Oldindan qilingan reja: be going to + fe’l.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Do you know the weather forecast?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: They say it ___ be sunny on Saturday.

gap.whyUz: Başorat (ob-havo) — will + fe’l: it will be sunny.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Sounds great. Can I come too?
lines.uz: Zör eşitiladi. Men ham borsam böladimi?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Of course! I ___ call you tonight with the details.
lines.uz: Albatta! Keçqurun qönğiroq qilib, tafsilotlarini aytaman.

gap.whyUz: Şu zahoti qabul qilingan qaror yoki va’da — will: I’ll call you.

note.titleUz: be going to va will — farqi
pointsUz: be going to — oldindan öylangan reja (I’m going to visit…).
will — başorat (It will rain) yoki şu zahoti qaror/va’da (I’ll help you).

examples.en: We are going to buy a new car.
It’s cold. I’ll close the window.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Have you ever worked in a hotel?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Yes, I ___. I worked at a hotel in Tashkent last year.
lines.uz: Ha, işlaganman. Ötgan yili Toşkentdagi mehmonxonada işladim.

gap.whyUz: Have you ever…? savoliga qisqa javob: Yes, I have / No, I haven’t.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Good. Have you finished your English course?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Not ___. I finish next month.

gap.whyUz: Inkor va savolda “yet” — hali: not yet.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: And have you used our booking system before?
lines.uz: Bizning bron qiliş tizimimizdan oldin foydalanganmisiz?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: No, I’ve ___ used it, but I learn quickly.
lines.uz: Yöq, heç foydalanmaganman, lekin tez örganaman.

gap.whyUz: “never” — heç qaçon: I’ve never used it.

note.titleUz: Present Perfect: ever, never, already, yet
pointsUz: have / has + fe’lning 3-şakli: I have worked, she has finished.
ever — savolda “heç”; never — “heç qaçon”.
already — allaqaçon (tasdiq); yet — hali (inkor/savol).

examples.en: Have you ever been to London?
I have already sent the email.

situationUz: Bir neça kundan beri boşingiz oğriyapti. Şifokor maslahat bermoqda.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: What’s the problem?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: I ___ a headache for three days.

gap.whyUz: Hozirgaça davom etayotgan holat: have had … for three days.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Do you sleep well? Do you drink enough water?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Not really. What ___ I do?

gap.whyUz: Maslahat söraş — should: What should I do?

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: You should sleep eight hours and drink more water. You mustn’t work late.
lines.uz: Sakkiz soat uxlang va köproq suv içing. Keç işlamasligingiz şart.

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Do I have ___ take any medicine?

gap.whyUz: Majburiyat: have to + fe’l → Do I have to take…?

note.titleUz: Modal fe’llar: should, must, have to
pointsUz: should — maslahat (You should rest).
must / mustn’t — qat’iy qoida (You mustn’t smoke here).
have to — taşqi majburiyat (I have to work on Saturday).
Modal fe’ldan keyin “to” qöyilmaydi: must go, should eat (have to bundan mustasno).

examples.en: You should see a dentist.
We have to wear a uniform.

situationUz: Mehmonlar uçun ovqat tayyorlaysiz va oziq-ovqat dökonidasiz.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Hello! Can I help you?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: Yes, please. I need ___ tomatoes and some rice.
lines.uz: Ha, iltimos. Menga bir neçta pomidor va bir oz guruç kerak.

gap.whyUz: Tasdiq gapda — some: I need some tomatoes.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: How many tomatoes would you like?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: A kilo, please. And how ___ rice do I need for six people?
lines.uz: Bir kilo, iltimos. Olti kişiga qança guruç kerak?

gap.whyUz: “rice” — sanalmaydi → how much; sanaladigan → how many.

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: About one kilo. Do you need any onions?

lines.speaker: b
lines.en: No, thanks. I’ve got a ___ of onions at home.

gap.whyUz: “a lot of” — köp (sanaladigan ham, sanalmaydigan ham).

note.titleUz: some / any, much / many, a lot of
pointsUz: some — tasdiqda, any — inkor va savolda.
many — sanaladigan (many apples), much — sanalmaydigan (much water).
a lot of — ikkalasi bilan ham işlaydi.

examples.en: Is there any milk?
We haven’t got much time.
